title: Behind the scenes of Scott Colom’s viral ‘pick another protein’ ad | CNN Politics
text:
Source: CNN

Russ Hudson of Columbus, Mississippi, became one of the unexpected stars of the 2026 midterms, with a feature role in an ad that’s since been viewedmore than 20 million times on X alone– tipping his head back and exclaiming, “sheeeit.”

“It’s been crazy. Like, I never expected it to do this,” Hudson told CNN in an interview, reflecting on the ad for Democratic Sen.-elect Scott Colom that helped spark one of the biggest political upsets of the election cycle.

Posted to social media on October 13, the ad features Hudson and other Mississippians rebuking incumbent GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith for suggesting there are many other proteins to chose from when pressed on high beef prices. “Pick another protein, sheeeit,” Hudson says in the spot as he grills burgers. “I’d rather pick another senator instead.”

“When I originally told Scott I would do it, I thought maybe like 100, maybe 1,000 views at most,” Hudson said. “I never expected it to do what it did. And I didn’t have TikTok. I literally had to download TikTok to see what all the hype was about because a bunch of my friends were sending messages like, ‘Dude, you’re like worldwide.’”

Hudson said that he’d been recognized in public a few times and asked for pictures, “like I’m some superstar or something.”

“So it’s a little weird. I’m not used to that, obviously,” he said.

Hudson, the father of a four-month-old infant and an Army veteran who served in Afghanistan, said that he’d known Colom for a decade, and that his sister had worked with him.

The initial plan called for Hudson’s father to appear in the ad, but he was reluctant to curse on camera, so the younger Russ volunteered.

“I just went to his mom’s house in the backyard, and we fired up the grill, and they gave me the lines, and we just rolled with it,” Hudson said.

For the signature line – the “s-h-e-e-e-i-t,” as Hudson spells it – he said they did about ten to fifteen takes, but that Colom said he nailed it on the third.

“That’s something we say. And my buddy was talking to me on the phone the other day, and he said something. I was like, ‘sheeeit!’ He was like, ‘There you go.’ It’s just a thing, man,” Hudson laughed.

Underscoring the ad’s point, Hudson also recalled saving the burgers he’s seen flipping on the grill. “[Colom] told me to save the burgers because beef prices were high. So, I didn’t want to waste them,” Hudson said.

Asked what he thought of the comment from Hyde-Smith that started it all, telling Mississippians to pick another protein, Hudson said that “it’s ridiculous.”

“We deserve better than that, and that’s why one of the reasons I really wanted to back Scott, you know, because I mean he wants to make things affordable for us here in Mississippi,” Hudson said.

He also considered the landmark victory, saying that “it’s pretty cool – I know it’s gonna go down in history. My mom keeps reminding me of that, and I’m just like, yeah, it’s pretty cool to be a part of that.”

“But the main thing is, is the goal was to help Scott win this election, and it did that,” he said, crediting the advertisement’s writers and producers for “all the work.”

As for what he’ll remember from the experience, Hudson paused for a moment.

“The Mississippi folks will appreciate this,” Hudson said, before referencing musician Doughbelly Stray. “[He] did a song one time that says, ‘My Mississippi ain’t on this map,’ and our Mississippi’s on this map now. So that’s what I remember from it as we put Mississippi on the map,” he said.

Ryan Sayles, the creative mind behind the ad, joined CNN’s “The Arena with Kasie Hunt” on Thursday and shared more details on the production.

Saying he wanted to bring a “Mississippi feel to it,” Sayles instructed the individuals reading the lines to “drag it out so people can really feel how you feel.” He also picked the catchy backing track – “Rapper’s Delight” by Sugarhill Gang – crediting his dad’s influence as a former DJ.

“I was a class clown, you know. I joke a lot, so I definitely think that this helped people look at it and say, “Oh man, this is funny,” but that’s really how I feel, you know,” Sayles said, underlining the importance of humor in political messaging. “Like it was funny, but it wasn’t funny, you know what I mean? It was a good way to just get attention and bring national attention to Mississippi.”

And Sayles praised Colom for his engagement with the process and willingness to take risks, saying that “he thinks about how he can reach people that normally wouldn’t be reached.”

Eight days after Election Day, CNNprojectedthat Colom would defeat Hyde-Smith, becoming the first Democrat elected to the US Senate in Mississippi in more than four decades. The outcome ranks as perhaps the most stunning upset in an election cycle full of historic wins as Democrats capitalized on sharp voter backlash to the Trump administration.

In a nod to the viral ad at his victory party last week, Colom stood at a lecternbehind a signthat read “picked another senator” as he thanked Mississippians for their support.
